subject: Able to estimate model with specific parameter values?

messages.author: c02e0f9087e29020
messages.subject: Able to estimate model with specific parameter values?
parts:
Hi guys, a naive question: is it possible to get stan to return model results (e.g. lp__) for a fixed set of parameter values?   I have my model set up to print lp__ after each iteration, and when I run stan for just 1 iteration it seems to give different results each time, despite having set fixed inits. Does this mean there is some sampling that goes on before the first iteration. If not I must be setting inits incorrectly.  I am trying to verify the model I have coded up in stan matches the one I have in R, so want to use specific parameter inputs.

Thanks - Nick

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Able to estimate model with specific parameter values?
parts:
You would need to also set the pseudo-random number seed to get replicatable results because the leapfrog step(s) for the first iteration involve randomness as to whether to move forward or backward. But if you are using R, then it is probably easier to evaluate the log_prob() function once for the model you compile.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Able to estimate model with specific parameter values?
parts:
Ben's suggestion is the right way to evaluate a log
probability in RStan.

As an aside, the 2.0 version of the command-line Stan outputs the
initial parameter values in the same stream as the warmup
and sample iterations (assuming "save_warmup=1" is used).

We'll have RStan do the same thing --- I don't know if the
current source version already does this (I also added a
feature request for instructions on building RStan from source :-)).

- Bob
